html:
SMTO-WEB-0001 — SMTO's web reader can't open addresses on a private network

GUID: 99fa6aea-cf27-4bde-a677-a12f86507a3d
Slug: web-blocked-private-target
Domain: WEB · Subsystem: web

What happened

  • The address points to a computer on a home, office or local network, not the public internet. SMTO's web reader only opens public websites, so it stopped before connecting. Nothing was read.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the address. If you meant a public website, correct it in your message, for example replace localhost or a 192.168… address with the site's public address. Addresses like localhost, 10.…, 172.16.… or 192.168.… always point inside a private network.
  2. If the site is internal to your organization, ask SMTO in the conversation to reach it through a Gateway or an HTTP connection set up for that service instead of the web reader. Those tools are meant for private services and have their own access checks.
  3. If a normal public site is refused, make sure the computer running SMTO isn't using a VPN, ad-blocking or filtering network that sends that site to a local address. SMTO refuses a site whenever its network lookup returns any private address, even for a well-known site.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads the page and shows its content, or the private service answers through the Gateway or HTTP connection.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address you used, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't ask anyone to turn off the private-address check or to hide the private address behind a public redirect.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The public-only Web transport refused the request because DNS for the target host returned at least one non-public (private, loopback, link-local, reserved or translation-range) address.

What this means

  • Public Web reads reject DNS answers containing any nonpublic target address before opening that target connection. The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.

Why this can happen

  • Public Web reads reject DNS answers containing any nonpublic target address before opening that target connection.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the requested host and resolved addresses on the execution host without bypassing the public-address guard.

How to fix it

  • open_get in src/agent_runtime/skills/web/transport.py rejects a hop when any resolved address fails _public(); check what the host resolves to from the Server (getent hosts or dig), including split-horizon DNS, VPN or DNS sinkholes returning 0.0.0.0. For intended private services use the HTTP connection or Gateway tools; keep the Web SSRF protection in place.
  • Use an approved native HTTP or Gateway route for the private service; retain Web SSRF protections.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended public URL resolves only to eligible addresses, or an approved private-service capability is used.

What not to do

  • Do not disable private-address checks or disguise a private destination with a public redirect.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic adds no retrieval. Read outcomes and retained receipts determine what evidence is available; an error does not establish the content of an unread source.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
